partially_covered.missing: No explicit enumeration or structured listing of all organization attributes; only basic address and GLN are modeled.
ValidationConstraint class present, but no explicit modeling of mandatory fields or D96A directory requirements.

cq_coverage.details: Most competency questions are directly answerable via well-defined classes and properties. CQ5 and CQ13 lack full attribute granularity and explicit validation requirements.

strengths: Deep, multi-level hierarchy reflects EDIFACT structure
weaknesses: Limited modeling of validation constraints and mandatory fields
Sections are subclasses of InvoiceMessage (should be composition, not inheritance)

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Missing domain or range for some inverse properties
P7: Subclass misuse for composition (Section < InvoiceMessage)
reasoner_risks: Hermit/Pellet may warn about asymmetric property overuse
No datatype issues detected (all datatypes are OWL 2 compliant)

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand Organization modeling to include all relevant attributes (e.g., contact info, identifiers, legal status) and enumerate them for CQ5.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves coverage and enables richer queries about organizations.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model mandatory D96A fields and validation requirements explicitly (e.g., property restrictions, SHACL shapes) for CQ13.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Ensures file format validity and supports automated validation.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Replace Section subclasses of InvoiceMessage with compositional object properties (hasSection) to avoid inheritance misuse.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Cleaner ontology structure and improved validator compatibility.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce General Class Axioms (GCAs) for advanced reasoning, e.g., define BuyerOrganization as an Organization with BuyerRole.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Richer semantic inference and improved query power.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add more detailed modeling for temporal aspects (e.g., transaction timing, validity periods).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Supports more advanced business process queries.

summary: The ontology provides comprehensive coverage of EDIFACT invoice structures, roles, and itemization, with correct use of reification and OWL 2 datatypes. Quality is high, but improvements are needed in modeling mandatory fields, validation constraints, and compositional relationships. Validator compatibility is strong, with only minor structural issues to address.
